topics.topic: Whether a zero-total confirmed publication may create an Expense and what initial allocation list it requires
questions: May a confirmed publication with `total_amount = 0` create an Expense, and if so must its initial allocation list contain at least one zero-valued instruction, or may it be empty?

quotes:
An expense creation from a confirmed recognition, once the route's project
guard of A4 has passed, is checked by the operation in this order:
recognition status `confirmed`, a supported contract version, the
authorized context's `portal.expense.manage` capability, its active project, a valid positive
`EUR` total, then the allocation instructions (shape, then sum equal to the
total, then each section belonging to the project), then replay by
`recognized_document_id`. Every refusal before the replay check answers
HTTP 422 with an empty body (`rules.http_router_backend.error_policy`), so
which of them failed first is not observable to the caller; a replay with
other content is the conflict of A8 (409).
judgement.why: State 2 requires a positive total for expense creation, so a zero-total publication is refused before its allocation list can matter.

topics.topic: Whether negative allocation totals may produce permitted negative derived expense values
questions: May exact aggregation of accepted negative allocations produce negative actual-material or Other-expenses values, and if so are those values additional permitted negative derived facts despite not being balances?

quotes:
Money is `Decimal` with 2 fraction digits, currency always `EUR`; rounding
  policy is a State 2 rule. Negative amounts never appear in stored records,
  with one named exception: an expense allocation amount (M26, M29);
  otherwise negative values exist only in derived balances.

An expense's instruction list must be non-empty and sum to the expense
  total (at creation the total is positive, so an empty list never sums);
  an individual amount is not otherwise constrained (zero and negative
  amounts are accepted and stored, M29).
judgement.why: Accepted negative allocation amounts can make the specified allocation-derived actual-material value negative, contradicting the convention that negative non-allocation values exist only in derived balances.

witness.initial: An active project has a manual budget with section A, no existing expenses, an authorized operator, and a viewer granted access to the project.
events: The operator submits a confirmed EUR 100 recognition result allocated as EUR -20 to section A and EUR 120 to `other_expenses`.
The viewer reads the project's budget and expense results.
outcomes: The allocation is accepted but section A cannot expose material actual of EUR -20, because negative values other than stored allocation amounts may exist only in derived balances.

The allocation is accepted and exact aggregation exposes section A material actual of EUR -20, because negative allocation amounts are accepted and section actual materials derive from included allocations.
witness.observer: The viewer sees whether section A's negative material actual is exposed; the operator also sees whether the submitted allocation can be represented consistently.
basis:
An expense is created when an authenticated staff member with mutation
capability on the project submits the confirmed recognition result with the
project and the allocation; a progress photo is published the same way.

An expense's instruction list must be non-empty and sum to the expense
  total (at creation the total is positive, so an empty list never sums);
  an individual amount is not otherwise constrained (zero and negative
  amounts are accepted and stored, M29).

An authenticated viewer sees the list of their assigned projects, opens one,
and reads: Registry project context, budget summary with source and ordered
sections, included and excluded confirmed expenses with `Other expenses`
separate, client-visible documents, work progress and completed work value,
payments and work balance, and the chronological photo gallery.
